messages:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: PAGERDUTY ALERT — Severity: P1
pagerduty-bot: Region: gcp-southamerica (southamerica-east1) — GPU allocation saturation detected. Autoscaler is stuck pending quota. Queue length rising for inference requests.

infra-oncall: Acked. Looking now. Which pool?

sre-maya: apptier-gpu-pool-02 showing 240/240 GPUs in use, pending attach requests piling up. Autoscaler shows 0 -> pending due to quota_exceeded. Runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/southamerica-gpu-quota

eng-runtime-kevin: Confirmed. Also seeing high queue latency and token rejections. Quick stats from the router: 
```
Queue depth: 1,200 -> 2,800 in 20m
Error rate (attach failures): 6.8% -> 13.2%
P95 latency: 420ms -> 1.8s
Affected models: rwd-instruct-13b-v1 (heavy), small embed workers
```

prod-support-tom: Customers reporting increased latency and some 503s. CS triage: 12 active tickets flagged as high. ETA on mitigation?

infra-oncall: Checking quota via gcloud: 
```
gcloud compute regions describe southamerica-east1 --project=redwood-prod --format="json(quotas)"
# snippet: GPUs (NVIDIA_T4): limit: 240, usage: 240
```

eng-runtime-kevin: Ok, it's a hard project-level GPU quota. Options: 1) Request quota raise (slow) 2) Reroute traffic to eu-west1 or us-west2 where capacity exists 3) Temporarily downscale non-critical batch jobs and reassign GPUs 4) Fallback to CPU-only pool for low-priority customers.

sre-maya: Initiating short-term mitigations: a) Pause nightly batch warm pools (non-critical) b) Start reroute rule to gradually shift 25% of inference traffic to eu-west1 with model fallback mapping c) Increase retry/backoff for attach ops.

eng-runtime-kevin: Deploying reroute now — creating a canary route in the router config: 
```
# router change (canary)
PATCH /api/v1/routes/canary
{ "match": "region:southamerica", "fallback_region": "eu-west1", "percent": 25 }
```

prod-support-tom: Notifying CS: telling customers we are mitigating, may see degraded perf while we reroute. @customer-success-ana please post update to affected accounts.

customer-success-ana: Drafting message now. Sending short notice: "We are experiencing increased latency in South America due to GPU capacity limits; we've started rerouting some requests to alternative regions to restore service. We'll update in 30m."

infra-oncall: Also creating temporary autoscaler override to allow scale up from reserved internal pool — patching autoscaler config: 
```
kubectl -n infra apply -f autoscaler-override.yaml
# override: allowBurst: true, burstPool: reserved-gpu-pool
```

eng-runtime-kevin: Applied override. Monitoring attach queue. If reserved pool attaches succeed, queue should drop.

sre-maya: Observed queue drop after canary rollout -> global queue depth: 2800 -> 1,100 in 10m. Error rate down to 7.2%. Some increased latency for canaryed traffic (eu-west1) ~2.4s.

prod-support-tom: CS reported initial relief; tickets reduced to 4 high severity. Good.

infra-oncall: Filing quota raise request with GCP (support case 01234567) but expect 24-72h for approval. This is not a quick fix.

eng-runtime-kevin: Longer-term actions proposed: a) Spread warm pools across regions b) Add multi-region attach fallback logic c) Consider project-level quota split across subprojects for burst capacity d) Improve model fallback to smaller variants automatically under attach failures.

sre-maya: Created follow-up ticket INFRA-9231 for multi-region warm pools and INFRA-9232 for quota-runbook improvements.

prod-support-tom: Oncall handover: @infra-oncall will be primary for next 4h, then hand to next shift. @eng-runtime-kevin please keep monitoring and post updates every 30m.

infra-oncall: Handing to night shift at 22:00 UTC. Current status: mitigations in place, queue reduced but not fully back to baseline. Customer impact: degraded P95 for some requests, ~4 high-priority customers affected with slower responses, no data loss.

eng-runtime-kevin: Next check in 30m. If queue increases again, plan B is to expand reroute to 50% and start cpu-fallback for non-SLA customers.

sre-maya: Adding runbook note: when project-level GPU quotas hit, prefer multi-region canary prior to scale overrides to limit global impact.

eng-runtime-kevin: Verified: canary stable, queue trending down. Will update thread after next metric push. :thumbsup:
